School is not a place to teach you how to learn or impart knowledge; it's a place that brainwashes you. The question then arises: What does it brainwash you in, and why would it do so? To answer this, we need some history. This class will cover a lot of history, but I'll briefly tell you about the three societies that first introduced mandatory free public schooling: Sparta, Aztecs, and Prussia.

Sparta was a small city-state in Greece around 3,000 years ago. They started putting children as young as five or six into schools where they were beaten by older kids. The Aztecs provided free compulsory education to all their children. Prussia, the system used today, was also focused on war.

What do Sparta, Aztecs, and Prussia have in common? All three were fundamentally war societies dedicated to defeating their neighbors. Sparta engaged in war-making; it's known for its Spartan warriors. The Aztecs were great war societies in Central America who defeated everyone and performed human sacrifices. Prussia had the greatest military in Europe for centuries.

So, why do we have schools? Schools are really good at preparing people for war. They teach kids how to handle the world. Why didn't other societies have schools before Sparta, Aztecs, and Prussia did? Because their societies were not engaged in constant warfare. 

If you're a parent with a child, what's the worst thing that could happen? Your child being taken away from you. School is designed to take your child away from you. If school was about learning, why don't parents and children go to school together? Because parents need to work to make money and survive.

School is about brainwashing. How do you brainwash someone? When separated from parents, you are more willing to be brainwashed because you feel insecure and afraid. Teachers become the authority figures, and your parents, who have also been brainwashed, agree with what the teachers say.

This is why our brains can be easily influenced by school; we trust teachers more when we're away from our secure parental environment.
